pages.title: Yunus Emre and Sufism
pages.content:
Yunus Emre was a famous Turkish poet and a Sufi from Anatolia. A Sufi is a person who aims to get closer to Allah by following Islamic mysticism. Sufis lead a way of life within the outer (visible) and inner rules of Islam. The outer part is related to the body’s acts of worship, while the inner side refers to the heart’s intentions and morality.

Sufis follow some moral rules: They try to become better people, they stay patient in hard times, and they give a lot to people in need. They expect nothing in return and do good to everyone without biases. They answer evil with kindness. Things like money, a high position and being famous are not important to them.

In addition to being a Sufi, Yunus Emre was one of the first to write and recite poems in simple Turkish. The words and phrases which he used helped develop a better literary Turkish. Yunus Emre is known as one of the founders of Turkish Sufi literature.

exercises.title: A Founder of a Literature
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the best answer from Chapter 1.
exercises.question: Why is Yunus Emre known as one of the founders of Turkish Sufi literature?
options: He wrote his poems in Arabic and Persian, the languages of the scholars of his time.
He was one of the first to write poems in simple Turkish, and his words helped develop literary Turkish.
He trained many famous Turkish poets in the tekkes of Anatolia and helped them improve their skills.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says Yunus Emre “was one of the first to write and recite poems in simple Turkish” and that the words and phrases he used “helped develop a better literary Turkish.” This is why he is called one of the founders of Turkish Sufi literature.

feedback.correct: Yes. He was an early poet in simple Turkish, and his language helped literary Turkish grow.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 1 again. Look for what Yunus Emre was “one of the first” to do and what his words helped to develop.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “By + -ing” Tell Us?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 1. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “A Sufi is a person who aims to get closer to Allah by following Islamic mysticism.” What does “by following Islamic mysticism” tell us?
options: why a person decides to become a Sufi
how a Sufi tries to reach this aim
what happens after a Sufi reaches this aim
when a person starts to follow this path
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The sentence is built in three steps. “A person who …” defines a person by what they do. “Aims to + verb” gives the aim (to get closer to Allah). “By + -ing” gives the method: The way the aim is reached (by following Islamic mysticism). Compare: “She improved her English by reading every day.”

feedback.correct: Correct. “By + -ing” names the way or method used to reach an aim.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentence again. The aim is “to get closer to Allah”. Does “by following …” give a reason, a time, or the way this aim is reached?

languageFocusExercises.title: Keep the List Parallel
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the list of moral rules?

errorItems.sentence: Sufis follow some moral rules: They try to become better people, they stay patient in hard times, and they gives a lot to people in need.
They answer evil with kindness. Things like money, a high position and being famous is not important to them.
In addition to be a Sufi, Yunus Emre was one of the first to write and say poems in simple Turkish.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The list of moral rules uses the same form every time: They try …, they stay …, they give …. Keeping the list parallel makes the rules sound like parts of one way of life. The subject “Things like money, a high position and being famous” is plural, so the verb is “are”. “In addition to” is a preposition, so it is followed by an -ing form: “In addition to being a Sufi …”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the list parallel, chose a plural verb and used -ing after “in addition to”.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the second paragraph of Chapter 1: Every rule in the list starts with “they” and a present simple verb. Then check the first words of the third paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It Another Way
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these lines about the Sufi?

transformItems.source: A Sufi is a person who aims to get closer to Allah by following Islamic mysticism.
transformItems.frame: A Sufi follows Islamic mysticism [blank] get closer to Allah.

transformItems.source: The words and phrases which he used helped develop a better literary Turkish.
transformItems.frame: He used words and phrases [blank] develop a better literary Turkish.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “By + -ing” gives the method; when the method comes first, “(in order) to + verb” gives the aim: “follows Islamic mysticism to get closer to Allah”. A “which/that” clause can describe the words and at the same time say what they did: “words and phrases which helped develop …”. “Help + verb” needs no “to”, but “help to + verb” is also correct. “Is known as” is the passive of “people know … as”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the meaning and changed the structure.
feedback.incorrect: Look at each sentence from Chapter 1 again: What is the aim, what did his words do, and how do people see him? Then fit that meaning into the new frame.

languageFocusExercises.title: Describe a Person, Practice, and Contribution
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about a teacher, artist or helper you know.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who is this person, and what do they do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong answer should form one short connected paragraph. Useful patterns include “a person who...”, “aims to... by -ing...”, parallel -ing forms, “without -ing...”, “in addition to...”, “which...”, “helped...”, and “is known as...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the ideas connected so the paragraph develops one clear description.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say who the person is: “… is a … who …”
discussionPrompts.example: My aunt Selma is a music teacher who works at a small village school.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say their aim and how: “She aims to … by …ing …”
discussionPrompts.example: She aims to make every child love music by teaching simple songs from many countries.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 3–4 — Give two or three things they believe in: “She believes in …ing, …ing and …ing.”
discussionPrompts.example: She believes in listening carefully, practising every day and helping weaker students. She also gives extra lessons without expecting anything in return.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 5–6 — Add more: “In addition to …, she … . She is known as …”
discussionPrompts.example: In addition to teaching, she writes short songs which the children sing at school events. She is known as the heart of the village school.

pages.title: His Language and Education
pages.content:
People love his works very much due to his style. It is neither too simple nor too complex. His works are very popular because they combine great literary quality with simple language. This plain language helps people understand his writings and sayings easily. The ideas in his poems teach important moral rules, and these rules still have a big influence on Turkish culture and society.

According to historical sources, he lived during the same era as important people like Haji Bektash Veli and Mevlana Jalal al-Din Rumi. He was born around 1240–1241 and died around 1320–1321. Some sources say that he received a good madrasa education and had a strong knowledge of Arabic, Persian, and the Islamic sciences of his time. But he also studied Allah’s love and morals at the tekke, which was a place where Sufi education was taught under the guidance of a sheikh (spiritual tutor).

exercises.title: Two Places of Learning
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 2.
exercises.question: Chapter 2 says that Yunus Emre studied Allah’s love and morals at the madrasa.
exercises.explanation: Some sources say he received a good madrasa education and had a strong knowledge of Arabic, Persian and the Islamic sciences. “But he also studied Allah’s love and morals at the tekke,” where Sufi education was taught under the guidance of a sheikh.

feedback.incorrect: Read the last two sentences of Chapter 2 again. Compare the two places where Yunus Emre studied and what he learned in each one.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Do These Phrases Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each phrase from Chapter 2 with its meaning in plain English.
languageFocusExercises.question: Why do people love Yunus Emre’s works?

matchingPairs.right: because of the way he writes

matchingPairs.left: neither too simple nor too complex
matchingPairs.right: in the middle: Not basic and not hard

matchingPairs.left: combine great literary quality with simple language
matchingPairs.right: are artistic and plain at the same time

matchingPairs.left: helps people understand his writings and sayings easily
matchingPairs.right: lets readers follow his words without effort

matchingPairs.left: still have a big influence on Turkish culture and society

correctAnswer.neither too simple nor too complex: in the middle: Not basic and not hard
correctAnswer.combine great literary quality with simp: are artistic and plain at the same time
correctAnswer.helps people understand his writings and: lets readers follow his words without effort
correctAnswer.still have a big influence on Turkish cu: continue to shape Turkish life today

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Due to + noun” gives a reason, like “because of”. “Neither … nor …” says no to both extremes, so the style is balanced. “Combine A with B” joins two qualities. “Help + person + verb” shows what something makes possible. “Still” shows that an influence from the past continues now.

feedback.correct: Good. You understood how the paragraph gives a reason, a balance, a combination, an effect and a continuing influence.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 2 again. Ask which phrase gives a reason, which one describes a balance, and which one says the influence continues today.

languageFocusExercises.title: Report History Carefully
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: How sure is the writer about Yunus Emre’s life?

formChoices.sentence: [choice] historical sources, he lived during the same era as important people like Haji Bektash Veli and Mevlana Jalal al-Din Rumi.
He was born [choice] 1240–1241 …
Some sources [choice] that he received a good madrasa education …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “According to + source” shows where the information comes from; “due to” gives a reason, not a source. “Around” shows an approximate date: The sources do not agree on one exact year, so the chapter gives a range. “Some sources say that …” shows that only part of the evidence reports this, so it is less certain. “Sources” is plural, so the verb is “say”; “tell” needs a person after it (tell someone).

feedback.correct: Correct. You kept the writer’s careful attitude to historical evidence.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2 again. Notice how the writer names the source, gives approximate dates, and shows that only some sources report the education.

languageFocusExercises.title: Two Kinds of Learning
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 2 with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where did Yunus Emre learn, and what was a tekke?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: … he received a good madrasa education and had a strong knowledge of Arabic, Persian, and the Islamic sciences of his time. But he [blank] studied Allah’s love and morals at the tekke, [blank] was a place where Sufi education was [blank] under the guidance of a sheikh (spiritual tutor).
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “But … also” adds a second kind of learning without cancelling the first: He studied at the madrasa and at the tekke. “Which” (not “who”) introduces extra information about a place or thing. “Was taught” is passive: The focus is on the education, not on the person who taught it.

feedback.correct: Well done. You added the second kind of learning and explained the tekke correctly.
feedback.incorrect: Check the last sentence of Chapter 2. Remember: “who” is for people, and after “was” we need a past participle for the passive.

languageFocusExercises.title: Write a Balanced, Evidence-Aware Profile
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about a writer, artist or teacher.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is good about this person, and where did they learn?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should develop one short profile rather than separate answers. Useful patterns include “due to...”, “neither too... nor too...”, “combine... with...”, “helps ... + verb”, “still...”, “according to...”, “some sources say that...”, “around...”, “but ... also...”, and a “which/where” clause when useful.

feedback.correct: Keep the evaluation, evidence, and learning experiences connected in one coherent profile.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 1–2 — Say what is good, and why: “… are neither too … nor too … . Due to this, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Amina Hassan’s stories are neither too long nor too short for young readers. Due to this balance, children can finish one story in a single evening.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Join two strengths: “… combine … with …”
discussionPrompts.example: Her books combine exciting adventures with useful lessons about friendship.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say where a fact comes from: “According to …, she was born around …”
discussionPrompts.example: According to her publisher, she was born around 1975 in a small town by the sea.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 5–6 — Add a second place of learning: “She also learned a lot at …”
discussionPrompts.example: She studied literature at university, but she also learned a lot at her grandmother’s house. It was a place where neighbors met every evening to tell old stories.

pages.title: Tekkes and Anatolia
pages.content:
At that time, tekkes were not only places for Sufi training. They were also important community organizations that helped people and brought them together. Furthermore, they received support from government officials. These places were very important for fine arts too, especially poetry. Many famous Turkish poets improved their skills in tekkes. Yunus Emre was also a great poet who trained under his spiritual tutor, Taptuk Emre.

Yunus Emre lived during the 13th and 14th centuries, which was a very difficult time in Anatolia. The Anatolian Seljuks were seriously weakened by the Babai revolts in the 13th century. While the negative effects of these revolts were still being felt, the defeat at Kösedağ took place. The defeat caused the Mongols' invasion of Anatolia. Because of these hard circumstances, Anatolia faced serious political, economic, and social problems. People were struggling to cope with these tough situations.

the spiritual tutor who trained Yunus

exercises.explanation: Chapter 3 says tekkes “were also important community organizations that helped people and brought them together,” and Yunus Emre “trained under his spiritual tutor, Taptuk Emre.” Then: “The Anatolian Seljuks were seriously weakened by the Babai revolts” and “The defeat caused the Mongols’ invasion of Anatolia.”

languageFocusExercises.title: Adding Information or Showing Cause?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Adding information, or cause and result? Put each sentence in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: How is each paragraph of Chapter 3 built?

items: They were also important community organizations that helped people and brought them together.
Furthermore, they received support from government officials.
These places were very important for fine arts too, especially poetry.

dragDropGroups.group: Shows a cause or a result
items: The Anatolian Seljuks were seriously weakened by the Babai revolts in the 13th century.
The defeat caused the Mongols' invasion of Anatolia.
Because of these hard circumstances, Anatolia faced serious political, economic, and social problems.

Adds more information: They were also important community organizations that helped people and brought them together.
Furthermore, they received support from government officials.
These places were very important for fine arts too, especially poetry.
Shows a cause or a result: The Anatolian Seljuks were seriously weakened by the Babai revolts in the 13th century.
The defeat caused the Mongols' invasion of Anatolia.
Because of these hard circumstances, Anatolia faced serious political, economic, and social problems.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The first paragraph builds a fuller picture of the tekkes: “not only … also”, “furthermore” and “too” add points, and “especially” highlights one example. The second paragraph builds a chain: “weakened by” names a cause, “caused” gives a result, and “because of + noun” links the hard circumstances to the problems.

feedback.correct: Correct. You saw that the first paragraph adds information and the second builds a cause-and-result chain.
feedback.incorrect: Look for adding words (also, furthermore, too) and for cause-and-result words (weakened by, caused, because of).

languageFocusExercises.title: Background and Event
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 3.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was still going on, and what happened suddenly?

formChoices.sentence: While the negative effects of these revolts [choice], the defeat at Kösedağ …
While the negative effects …, the defeat at Kösedağ [choice].
People were struggling to [choice] these tough situations.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “While” + past continuous sets up a background situation that was still going on. The effects did not feel anything; people felt them, so the form is passive: “were still being felt”. The new, finished event is in the past simple: “the defeat … took place”. “Cope with + noun” means to manage a difficult situation.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the continuing background from the new event.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3. Which part was still continuing, and which event happened during it? Remember that “cope” needs “with” before a noun.

languageFocusExercises.title: Same Cause, New Sentence
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say why things changed?

transformItems.source: The Anatolian Seljuks were seriously weakened by the Babai revolts in the 13th century.
transformItems.frame: The Babai revolts [blank] the Anatolian Seljuks in the 13th century.

transformItems.source: The defeat caused the Mongols' invasion of Anatolia.
transformItems.frame: The Mongols invaded Anatolia [blank] the defeat.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: A passive sentence with “by” puts the affected side first: “The Seljuks were weakened by the revolts.” The active sentence puts the cause first: “The revolts weakened the Seljuks.” “X caused Y” can also be said the other way round: “Y happened because of / as a result of X.”

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the same cause and result in a new structure.
feedback.incorrect: Ask who or what did the action in each sentence from Chapter 3, and what happened because of it. Then fit that into the new frame.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain Change in a Difficult Period
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about a place or group that faced a change.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened, and how did people cope?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should form one connected account. Useful patterns include “not only ... but also...”, “furthermore”, “too”, “especially”, “while ... was/were still...”, “caused...”, “because of...”, and “struggle to cope with...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the ideas connected so the description develops into a clear sequence of pressure, change, and response.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 1–2 — Describe the place: “… is not only … but also …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our town market is not only a place for shopping but also a place where neighbors meet. Furthermore, it gives work to many local farmers.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give an example: “… especially …”
discussionPrompts.example: Many people love it, especially older people who live alone.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Add a new event: “While … were still …, …”
discussionPrompts.example: While the farmers were still preparing for the spring season, a big storm destroyed part of the market roof.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 5–6 — Give the cause, the result and how people coped.
discussionPrompts.example: The storm caused many stalls to close for a month. People struggled to cope with the loss, so they opened small stalls in the school yard.

pages.title: The Babai Revolts
pages.content:
If we take a closer look at this historical atmosphere, we can better understand Anatolia—the land where Yunus Emre lived and recited his unforgettable verses.

The rule of the Anatolian Seljuk Sultan Ala al-Din Kayqubad I (1220–1237) was the most powerful and brilliant period of the Seljuks. He expanded the country’s borders and established a navy in the Mediterranean and Black Seas. At the time of his death, the Seljuks were the most powerful and largest state in the Middle East. However, his son Kaykhusraw II (1237–1246) did not rule the country well, so Seljuk money and social life began to get worse. The Mongol invasion caused many people to migrate to Anatolia from Central Asia, which totally turned the lives of the local people upside down. At the beginning of the 13th century, the Turkmen population grew in Anatolia. However, Kaykhusraw II’s failure to manage this situation worsened the social and economic chaos.

exercises.title: From Strength to Hard Times
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the best answer from Chapter 4.
exercises.question: According to Chapter 4, why did Seljuk money and social life begin to get worse?
options: Ala al-Din Kayqubad I expanded the borders and built a navy in two seas.
Kaykhusraw II ruled poorly and could not manage the growing Turkmen population.
Many Turkmen people left Anatolia and moved back to Central Asia.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 says “his son Kaykhusraw II (1237–1246) did not rule the country well,” and that his “failure to manage this situation worsened the social and economic chaos.” Ala al-Din Kayqubad I’s rule was the most powerful period, and people migrated to Anatolia from Central Asia, not away from it.

feedback.correct: Yes. The problem was that the son did not rule well, not his father’s strong rule.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second half of Chapter 4 again, from “However, his son …”. Who ruled after Ala al-Din Kayqubad I, and what did he fail to do?

languageFocusExercises.title: Why Does the Chapter Begin with “If”?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the first sentence of Chapter 4. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “If we take a closer look at this historical atmosphere, we can better understand Anatolia …” What is the writer telling the reader?
options: People must study history before they are allowed to read about Yunus Emre.
Learning about the history of that time will help us understand the place better.
The writer is not sure that the history of Anatolia is true.
Anatolia was easier to understand in the past than it is today.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “If + present simple, … can + verb” gives a condition and a possible result. The condition is an approach (taking a closer look at the history), and “can better understand” is what becomes possible if we follow it. The writer uses “we” to invite the reader to look at the history together before the chapter tells it.

feedback.correct: Correct. The “if” part gives an approach, and “can” shows the understanding that becomes possible.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentence again. The “if” part is not a rule or a doubt. What becomes possible when we look closely at the history?

languageFocusExercises.title: Strength, Change and Place
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: When was the state strong, and what changed?

formChoices.sentence: The rule of the Anatolian Seljuk Sultan Ala al-Din Kayqubad I (1220–1237) was [choice] period of the Seljuks.
[choice] his son Kaykhusraw II (1237–1246) did not rule the country well …
… Anatolia—the land [choice] Yunus Emre lived and recited his unforgettable verses.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The superlative “the most + adjective” with “the” evaluates Ala al-Din Kayqubad I’s rule as the highest point of the Seljuks. “However” turns the story in a new direction: After the strongest period, things get worse. “Where” begins a clause about a place (the land where he lived); “which” would need a subject or object after it, and “when” is for time.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the superlative, the contrast word and the place word.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 4 again. Is the sentence praising the best period, turning to a change, or describing a place?

languageFocusExercises.title: Same Cause, New Sentence
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say why things got worse?

transformItems.source: The Mongol invasion caused many people to migrate to Anatolia from Central Asia …
transformItems.frame: Many people migrated to Anatolia from Central Asia [blank] the Mongol invasion.

transformItems.source: … Kaykhusraw II’s failure to manage this situation worsened the social and economic chaos.
transformItems.frame: The social and economic chaos got worse because Kaykhusraw II [blank] this situation.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “X caused people to + verb” puts the cause first. With “because of / as a result of + noun”, the result comes first and the cause comes at the end. “Someone’s failure to + verb” is a noun phrase; as a clause it becomes “someone failed to + verb” (or “did not manage to …”). “Worsened” means “made worse”, so the result can be said as “got worse”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the same cause and result in a new structure.
feedback.incorrect: Ask what the cause is in each sentence from Chapter 4 and what happened because of it. Then fit that cause into the new frame.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain How a Situation Changes Over Time
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about a place that changed over time.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was the place like before, and what changed?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should develop one coherent account. Useful language from the chapter includes “If we... we can...”, superlative descriptions such as “the most...”, “however”, “because of...”, “caused ... to...”, “which...”, “began to...”, and “failure to ... worsened...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the time change and the cause-result links explicit so the paragraph reads as one explanation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Start: “If we look at …, we can better understand …”
discussionPrompts.example: If we look at the history of our school library, we can better understand why reading is so popular here today.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Describe a good time: “… years ago, … was the busiest …”
discussionPrompts.example: Twenty years ago, the library was the busiest and most popular room in the school.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Show a change: “However, …”
discussionPrompts.example: However, after the computer room opened, fewer students visited it.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 4–6 — Give a cause, its effect and how it ended.
discussionPrompts.example: Because of this, the school stopped buying new books, and the old shelves caused even more students to stay away. Last year, a new reading club started, and the library became busy again.

pages.title: Kösedağ and Destruction
pages.content:
Because of many economic and social problems, the Turkmen people were looking for a way out and started a revolt against the state. They followed spiritual leaders called 'Baba' because they believed these leaders would save them. The rebellion spread rapidly; the Turkmen achieved significant success. In the end, the Seljuk forces put an end to the rebellion with great difficulty and defeated the rebels with swords.

However, this situation gave the Mongols in Azerbaijan the courage to attack the Seljuk Empire. In 1242, the Mongols captured Erzurum and killed its people. This disaster caused deep sorrow and fear among the Seljuk people. Finally, in 1243, the Seljuk army and the Mongols clashed at Kösedağ, 80 km northeast of Sivas. The Mongols used the classic false retreat and circling tactic. Thus, they easily defeated the Seljuks. After that, the Mongols destroyed and raided Sivas, Kayseri, and Erzincan, leaving not a single stone standing.

__historical_entity__:yunus-sivas
__historical_entity__:yunus-kayseri
__historical_entity__:yunus-erzincan
__historical_entity__:yunus-azerbaijan

__historical_entity__:yunus-mongols
__historical_entity__:yunus-turkmens
Organized, often violent action against a government or ruler.
Took control of a place by force.
A feeling of deep sadness.
Fought or came into violent conflict.

hotspots.title: Kösedağ
hotspots.description: In 1243 the Mongols defeated the Seljuk army at Kösedağ with a false retreat.

hotspots.title: Destruction
hotspots.description: After the battle, the Mongols destroyed and raided Sivas, Kayseri and Erzincan.

exercises.title: The Road to Kösedağ
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 5 in the right order.
exercises.question: In what order did these events happen?

sequencingItems.text: The Turkmen started a revolt and followed spiritual leaders called ‘Baba’.
The Seljuk forces ended the rebellion with great difficulty.
The Mongols in Azerbaijan attacked and captured Erzurum.
The Seljuk army and the Mongols clashed at Kösedağ.
The Mongols raided Sivas, Kayseri and Erzincan.

exercises.explanation: The revolt came first, and the Seljuk forces ended it “with great difficulty.” This “gave the Mongols in Azerbaijan the courage to attack”: they captured Erzurum in 1242, defeated the Seljuks at Kösedağ in 1243, and after that raided Sivas, Kayseri and Erzincan.

feedback.correct: Well done. The hard fight against the revolt left the Seljuks weak, and this opened the way for the Mongol attacks.
feedback.incorrect: Follow the time words in Chapter 5: “In the end”, “In 1242”, “Finally, in 1243” and “After that”.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Would” Show?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the words from Chapter 5. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “… they believed these leaders would save them.” What does “would save” tell us?
options: The leaders really saved the Turkmen in the end.
The Turkmen used to be saved by the leaders again and again.
At that time, the Turkmen expected to be saved in the future.
The Turkmen politely asked the leaders to save them.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Would” is the past form of “will”. After a past verb like “believed”, it shows a future that people expected at that time: They thought, “These leaders will save us.” The sentence does not say that the leaders really saved them. In fact, the chapter says the Seljuk forces put an end to the rebellion.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Believed … would” reports what people expected, seen from that time in the past.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 5 again. Did the rebellion succeed in the end? So is “would save” a fact or an expectation?

languageFocusExercises.title: Linking Events in a Chain
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 5 with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened, and what did it lead to?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: [blank], this situation gave the Mongols in Azerbaijan the courage to attack the Seljuk Empire. In 1242, the Mongols captured Erzurum and killed its people. This disaster [blank] deep sorrow and fear among the Seljuk people. … The Mongols used the classic false retreat and circling tactic. [blank], they easily defeated the Seljuks.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “However” marks an unexpected turn: The Seljuks had just ended the rebellion, but this same situation gave the Mongols courage. “Cause + noun” shows what an event produced (“caused deep sorrow and fear”); we do not say “made sorrow”. “Thus” introduces a result of what was just described: The tactic worked, so they won easily. “Because” cannot stand alone with a comma before a sentence.

feedback.correct: Well done. You linked the turn, the emotional result and the military result.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5 again. Which blank starts a surprising new development, and which one follows from the tactic?

languageFocusExercises.title: Because or Because Of?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you choose between “because” and “because of”?

errorItems.sentence: Because many economic and social problems, the Turkmen people were looking for a way out and started a revolt against the state.
They followed spiritual leaders called 'Baba' because of they believed these leaders would save them.
After that, the Mongols destroyed and raided Sivas, Kayseri, and Erzincan, left not a single stone standing.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Because of” is followed by a noun phrase (“because of many economic and social problems”). “Because” is followed by a clause with a subject and a verb (“because they believed …”). After a comma, an -ing clause can add the result of the main action: “…, leaving not a single stone standing.”

feedback.correct: Well done. You chose “because of” before a noun, “because” before a clause, and an -ing form for the result.
feedback.incorrect: Look at what comes after each linking word: a noun phrase or a subject + verb? Then check the sentences in Chapter 5.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a Chain of Pressure, Belief, and Result
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about a hard time for a town or village.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did people hope for, and what really happened?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should read as one connected explanation. Useful language from the chapter includes “because of...”, “were looking for...”, “started...”, “because they believed... would...”, “however”, “caused...”, “thus”, and “after that”.

feedback.correct: Keep the relationships explicit so each sentence develops the previous one.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the problem: “Because of …, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Because of heavy rain all week, the river near our village rose very quickly.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what people were doing: “Families were …ing …”
discussionPrompts.example: Families were looking for a safe place and started to move their animals to higher fields.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what they believed: “They believed that … would …”
discussionPrompts.example: They believed that the old bridge would protect the village from the water.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Add a surprise: “However, …”
discussionPrompts.example: However, the bridge broke on Friday night.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 5–6 — Give the result: “This caused … . Thus, …”
discussionPrompts.example: This caused a flood in the lower streets. Thus, many families had to stay at the school for a week.

options: a long siege of the city
the false retreat and circling tactic

pages.title: Chaos in Anatolia
pages.content:
The men were killed by the sword. The women and children were taken captive and forced to go with the Mongols. They caused a lot of destruction, sadness, and misery everywhere they went. After these cruel raids, cities were deserted. Yunus Emre lived during a time when the Mongol army invaded Anatolia.

These events created an atmosphere of panic in Anatolia that had never been seen before. Finally, an agreement was made with the Mongols, but in time the Seljuks became dependent on them. The Seljuk sultans acted almost like government officials for the Mongols. A significant part of state income began to be sent to the Mongols every year. However, this tax increased continuously and this made both the state and the people poorer. After 1277, the Mongols began to administer Anatolia through the commanders and governors that they sent. And in 1308, the lands of Anatolia were directly attached to the Ilkhanate Empire (the Mongol state centred in Iran).

__historical_entity__:yunus-iran
__historical_entity__:yunus-yunus-emre

__historical_entity__:yunus-mongols

Relying on another person or power.

hotspots.description: The raids brought death, captivity, deserted cities and panic.

exercises.title: The Cost of Dependence
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the best answer from Chapter 6.
exercises.question: After the agreement with the Mongols, why did the Seljuk state and its people become poorer?
options: The Seljuk sultans spent most of the state’s income on a new army to fight against the Mongols.
The Mongols broke the agreement and attacked Anatolia again every year.
A large part of the state’s income went to the Mongols every year, and this tax kept rising.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “A significant part of state income began to be sent to the Mongols every year. However, this tax increased continuously and this made both the state and the people poorer.”

feedback.correct: Right. The yearly payment to the Mongols kept growing, so the state and its people became poorer.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of the second paragraph of Chapter 6 again. Look for what happened to the state’s income every year.

languageFocusExercises.title: Who Is the Subject?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Does the subject do the action, or does the action happen to it? Sort the sentences.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who does the action in each sentence?

items: They caused a lot of destruction, sadness, and misery everywhere they went.
These events created an atmosphere of panic in Anatolia …
After 1277, the Mongols began to administer Anatolia …

dragDropGroups.group: Passive: The action happens to the subject
items: The men were killed by the sword.
The women and children were taken captive …
… in 1308, the lands of Anatolia were directly attached to the Ilkhanate Empire …

Active: The subject acts: They caused a lot of destruction, sadness, and misery everywhere they went.
These events created an atmosphere of panic in Anatolia …
After 1277, the Mongols began to administer Anatolia …
Passive: The action happens to the subje: The men were killed by the sword.
The women and children were taken captive …
… in 1308, the lands of Anatolia were directly attached to the Ilkhanate Empire …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The passive is “was/were + past participle”. It puts the people or places that suffered in first position: the men, the women and children, the lands of Anatolia. The doer is often not named because the focus is on what happened to the victims. Note: “by the sword” names the weapon, not the doer.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the sentences about the doers from the sentences about those affected.
feedback.incorrect: Look for “was/were + past participle” (killed, taken, attached). In those sentences the subject does not act; something happens to it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Step by Step to Dependence
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 6.
languageFocusExercises.question: How did the Seljuk state slowly lose its power?

formChoices.sentence: Finally, an agreement was made with the Mongols, but in time the Seljuks [choice] dependent on them.
The Seljuk sultans acted [choice] government officials for the Mongols.
A significant part of state income began [choice] to the Mongols every year.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “In time … became + adjective” shows a slow change of state in the past. “Almost like + noun” compares: The sultans were not really Mongol officials, but they behaved nearly as if they were. The income did not send anything; someone sent it, so the passive infinitive is needed: “began to be sent”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You showed the change of state, the comparison and the passive process.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 6 again. Did the income send something, or was it sent? Is the chapter saying the sultans were officials, or nearly like them?

languageFocusExercises.title: Keep the Meaning, Change the Focus
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these lines from Chapter 6?

transformItems.source: … this tax increased continuously and this made both the state and the people poorer.
transformItems.frame: Because this tax increased continuously, both the state and the people [blank].

transformItems.source: After 1277, the Mongols began to administer Anatolia through the commanders and governors that they sent.
transformItems.frame: After 1277, Anatolia [blank] by the Mongols through the commanders and governors that they sent.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Make + object + comparative adjective” (made the people poorer) shows a result. With the affected people as the subject, the same result is “the people became / got poorer”. In the passive, the object of the active sentence (Anatolia) becomes the subject, and the doer can follow with “by”: “Anatolia began to be administered by the Mongols.”

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the result and changed the focus of the sentence.
feedback.incorrect: Ask who or what was affected in each sentence from Chapter 6. Put that person or place first and use “became + adjective” or “(began to) be + past participle”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Describe a Process of Losing Control
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about a group that slowly loses control.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does the group lose control, step by step?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should develop as one short process. Useful language from the chapter includes “was/were + past participle”, “in time”, “became...”, “almost like...”, “began to be...”, “however”, “made ... + adjective”, “through...”, and “was/were directly attached to...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the stages connected so the reader can see who is affected, how the situation changes, and what the final consequence is.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what happened to the group: “… was bought by …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our local football club was bought by a large company in 2015.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Show a change: “In time, … became …”
discussionPrompts.example: In time, the club became dependent on the company’s money.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Compare: “… acted almost like …”
discussionPrompts.example: The club manager acted almost like an employee of the company.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Show a new start: “Soon, … began to be …”
discussionPrompts.example: Soon, all important decisions began to be made in the company’s office in the capital.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 5–6 — Give the result: “However, … . This made …”
discussionPrompts.example: However, the company cut the budget every year, and this made the club weaker. In 2022, the club was finally closed.

beforeYouRead.quote: After these cruel raids, cities were deserted.

I can describe what happened to people without naming who did it.

pages.title: Yunus as a Wise Dervish
pages.content:
Anatolia was experiencing total chaos. During the same period, the shaykhs from the regions of Turkestan, Khorasan and Iran came to Anatolia under Mongol pressure. These shaykhs trained dervishes in their teachings. These dervishes were influential among nomads. They were spreading a simple understanding of Islam and establishing popular Sufism.

So in such an environment, Yunus Emre also appeared as a wise Sufi and dervish and traveled around Anatolia. As a Sufi, he helped people make sense of life during those hard days. Poetry was his most influential tool.

Yunus’s understanding of Sufism comes from the Qur’an and the Prophet’s (pbuh) Sunnah. He was also inspired by the ideas and experiences of earlier Muslim Sufis.

__historical_entity__:yunus-turkestan
__historical_entity__:yunus-khorasan
__historical_entity__:yunus-iran
__historical_entity__:yunus-yunus-emre
__historical_entity__:yunus-mongols
A strong force that pushes people to do something.
Members of a Sufi group who follow a spiritual path.
Having a strong effect on what people think or do.
People who move from place to place rather than living permanently in one place.

hotspots.title: Wise Sufi
hotspots.description: Yunus traveled around Anatolia and helped people make sense of life in hard days.

hotspots.title: Poetry
hotspots.description: Poetry was his most influential tool.

exercises.title: Poetry in Hard Times
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the best answer from Chapter 7.
exercises.question: How did Yunus Emre respond to the hard days in Anatolia?
options: He traveled around Anatolia and used poetry to help people make sense of life.
He left Anatolia and went to Khorasan to study with the shaykhs there.
He trained the dervishes who spread a simple understanding of Islam among nomads.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7 says Yunus Emre “appeared as a wise Sufi and dervish and traveled around Anatolia” and “helped people make sense of life during those hard days. Poetry was his most influential tool.” It was the shaykhs from Turkestan, Khorasan and Iran who trained dervishes.

feedback.correct: Yes. In a time of total chaos, he traveled and used poetry to help people.
feedback.incorrect: The first paragraph of Chapter 7 is about the shaykhs and their dervishes. Read the second paragraph to find what Yunus himself did.

languageFocusExercises.title: A Foundation and an Inspiration
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the last two sentences of Chapter 7. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Yunus’s understanding of Sufism comes from the Qur’an and the Prophet’s (pbuh) Sunnah. He was also inspired by the ideas and experiences of earlier Muslim Sufis.” How are the two sources different?
options: The earlier Sufis are the foundation, and the Qur’an and the Sunnah are an extra inspiration.
Both sentences say exactly the same thing in different words.
The Qur’an and the Sunnah are the foundation, and the earlier Sufis are an extra inspiration.
The second sentence shows that Yunus disagreed with the earlier Sufis.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Comes from” names the origin or foundation of something. “Was also inspired by” adds a second, additional influence: Ideas and experiences that encouraged him. The word “also” shows that this influence is added to the foundation, not placed above it.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Comes from” gives the foundation, and “was also inspired by” adds another influence.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verbs: “comes from” and “was also inspired by”. Which one names the origin, and which one adds something with “also”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about the dervishes?

errorItems.sentence: They were spreading a simple understanding of Islam and established popular Sufism.
These dervishes were influential between nomads.
As a Sufi, he helped people making sense of life during those hard days.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: In “were spreading … and establishing …”, both verbs share “were”, so both need the -ing form: two activities going on at the same time. We are influential “among” a group of people. “Help + person + base verb” shows what someone makes possible for others: “helped people make sense of life”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the parallel -ing forms, the preposition and the verb pattern correct.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with Chapter 7: the end of the first paragraph and the second paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Time, Pressure and Response
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 7 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was happening, and how did Yunus Emre help?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Anatolia was experiencing total chaos. [blank] the same period, the shaykhs from the regions of Turkestan, Khorasan and Iran came to Anatolia [blank] Mongol pressure. … So in [blank] an environment, Yunus Emre also appeared as a wise Sufi and dervish and traveled around Anatolia. … Poetry was his [blank] influential tool.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “During + noun” places an event inside a period; “while” needs a clause (while + subject + verb). “Under … pressure” shows the force behind an action. “Such an environment” points back to everything described before: chaos, pressure and new teachers. “His most influential tool” is a superlative: Poetry was the strongest of his ways of reaching people.

feedback.correct: Well done. You placed the events in time and linked the situation with Yunus’s response.
feedback.incorrect: Check the first two paragraphs of Chapter 7. Remember: “during” comes before a noun, and a superlative after “his” needs “most”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Response from Its Context
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about someone who helped people in a hard time.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was the problem, and how did the person help?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Useful language from the chapter includes “during the same period”, “under ... pressure”, “were ...-ing and ...-ing”, “so in such an environment”, “helped people make sense of...”, “influential among...”, “most influential tool”, “comes from...”, and “was inspired by...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the sentences connected so the context leads naturally to the response, the tool, and the sources of influence.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the problem: “Last winter, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Last winter, heavy snow closed the roads to our village for three weeks.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what people were doing: “During that time, … were …ing …”
discussionPrompts.example: During that time, families were sharing food and checking on older neighbors.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Bring in the person: “So …, … also offered help.”
discussionPrompts.example: So in such a situation, a retired nurse called Mrs. Karim also offered her help.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say how she helped: “She helped people … . Her … was her most useful tool.”
discussionPrompts.example: She helped people stay calm and healthy, and her phone was her most influential tool.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 5–6 — Say where her ideas come from: “Her way … comes from … . She was also inspired by …”
discussionPrompts.example: Her way of working comes from her long experience in hospitals. She was also inspired by her mother, who cared for sick people in the same village.

beforeYouRead.quote: During the same period, the shaykhs from the regions of Turkestan, Khorasan and Iran came to Anatolia under Mongol pressure.
